Jazz in Australia is alive and well with players like Tom Baker. Tom is a native Californian but has resided in Australia since the age of 19. A multi- instrumentalist and singer, his enthusiasm on stage makes him a sought after player at jazz gatherings around the world. His self stated mission is to keep the Swing music of the ‘30s and ‘40s alive, and he leads two traditional jazz bands at home. He has recorded for Stomp Off and Arbors Records and recently teamed up with Australian jazz legend Bob Barnard for his latest CD. He is also famous in jazz circles for his Mexican, French and Indian culinary creations.
Tom was interviewed on September 13, 1997 at the Allegheny Jazz Party in Chautauqua, New York by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
We’re filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. My name is Monk Rowe and it’s my pleasure to have Tom Baker as my guest here in Chautauqua, New York. Welcome.
